I need to fill the hollow 1 shape completely while clearing out the interior of the 7 rectangle, so I'm tracing through each row to mark which cells belong to the 1 and identifying its enclosed empty spaces to fill in.

Tracing the flood-fill logic row by row: checking which zero cells connect to the outside boundary versus which are truly interior pockets trapped by the 1 shape, so I can determine exactly which cells need to become 1.

Row 12 just has the boundary cells filled in.

content.text:
I need to work out the transformations: shape 7 goes from filled diamond to hollow outline, shape 5 goes from hollow rectangle to filled, shape 9 goes from hollow to filled, and shape 3 goes from filled blob to outline only. For shape 7's diamond, I'm mapping out its rows and figuring out which cells are on the boundary versus interior, since only boundary cells should remain once it's hollowed out.

For the small diamond, I find that only the single center cell counts as interior surrounded on all four sides, so that one becomes empty while the rest stay as outline. Shapes 5 and 9 are simple since I just need to fill every cell in their rows and columns. For shape 3's larger blob, I'm going row by row checking each cell's four neighbors to determine which ones are fully interior and should be cleared, leaving only the boundary cells to form the outline.

Continuing to fill in the boundary and interior values row by row, finishing out rows 18 through 23 with their boundary markers of 3 and interior zeros.
